posts.text:
Growing up in Indonesia, I learned one unwritten rule about jobs: never ask about the salary first.

You wait. You show you are serious, hardworking, grateful for the chance. If you bring up money too early, people might think you are only in it for the pay. Sungkan, we call it. That polite hesitation runs deep.

So when I moved to Singapore, the hiring signs surprised me.

Outside restaurants and retail shops, the salary is written right on the notice. The role, the hours, and how much per month. No guessing, no awkward question.

Here, the mindset seems different. Putting the number upfront saves time for both sides. The candidate knows straight away if it works for them. The employer only talks to people who are already fine with the range.

It made me rethink what I grew up with: being clear is not the same as being rude.

I am still unlearning the sungkan. Old habits take a while.

So I am curious:
A. Salary upfront, from the first conversation
B. Talk about it later, once there is a fit

Which feels more comfortable to you, and where did you pick up that habit?

📌 Strengthening surveillance and information sharing to address the cross-border spread of resistant organisms, including through food supply chains and the environment.
📌 Building on existing regional mechanisms to conduct joint risk assessments and develop shared priorities ahead of the 2029 UN High-Level Meeting on AMR.
